key_insight: Marginal Advantage Accumulation (MAA) turns noisy batch-by-batch feedback into a cross-batch evidence stream so memory operations can be judged by consistent advantage rather than accidental hits.
engineering_relevance: For memory-driven agents, MAA offers a post-processing layer that improves trace distillation reliability without changing the base model, while also cutting optimization-phase token use by about 75%.
method: Build differential signals that make batch feedback comparable
Accumulate signed per-operation evidence with EMA
Merge semantically identical traces to preserve cross-batch identity
evidence_signal: The abstract reports best results in 14 of 16 settings across 4 benchmarks and 4 target models, outperforming batch-level baselines and often matching or beating online methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly aligning and merging semantic identities across batches, which may be difficult when traces are noisy or operation semantics drift.
paper_title: Marginal Advantage Accumulation for Memory-Driven Agent Self-Evolution
